title: Point classes over a fixed base point via normalized closure
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], let $f:X	o S$ be any morphism of schemes, and let $s\in S$. Give $Z_s=\overline{\{s\}}$ its reduced closed subscheme structure [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-reduced-scheme]; it is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $
u_s:N_s=Z_s^
u	o Z_s\hookrightarrow S$ be its normalization in $\kappa(s)$ [def-sc-normalization, def-weil-residue-field], and put $Y_s=X	imes_SN_s$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $V_f$ be the vanishing topos [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles], with second projection $p_2:V_f	o S_{\mathrm{Et}}$. A point means a geometric morphism from $\mathbf{Set}$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. Let $\mathcal P_s$ be the full subcategory of points $p$ of $V_f$ such that $p_2p$ is represented by a geometric point of $S$ whose underlying scheme point is $s$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. There is a bijection $	heta_s$ from the isomorphism classes of $\mathcal P_s$ to $|Y_s|$, compatible with their projections to $|X|$, for which
$$\exists\,(q\Rightarrow p)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad	heta_s([p])\in\overline{\{	heta_s([q])\}}\qquad(p,q\in\mathcal P_s).$$
Here the $2$-morphism is a $2$-morphism of points in $V_f$, as defined in [def-trf-geometric-morphism], and the closure on the right is Zariski closure in $Y_s$. In particular this relation is antisymmetric on isomorphism classes in $\mathcal P_s$. No finite-type hypothesis on $f$ and no finiteness hypothesis on $
u_s$ are imposed.

This is the geometric classification in that proof, before its finiteness argument.
